record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Forchhammer to lend fossil and recent cirripedes, especially Arctic specimens, so he can compare them with Steenstrup’s fossils before beginning the Sessile species. The return address and planned carriage to Copenhagen are explicit.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 25 September [1849], XML exact day. This is a Darwin outgoing request; dispatch and any later physical receipt of specimens remain separate.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Forchhammer and Steenstrup are named recipients/authorities, while the requested specimens are not yet received.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The request supplies a distinctive antecedent for Forchhammer’s later copy-book record 1270; the response direction is 1270→1255.

evidence.quote: I shd be particularly glad to compare them with Steentrup’s fossil species.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Forchhammer to forward an enclosed letter to Sven Lovén, support the request for an Alepas squalicola specimen, and identify an Eschricht Cineras from Oxford.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [30 September 1849], XML exact day. The enclosure’s dispatch and Lovén’s possible response are not shown.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Lovén and Eschricht are third-party scientific contacts and the enclosure is absent from the preserved body.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This initiates a Lovén/specimen exchange; neither 1270’s Steenstrup parcel nor another target answers it.

record_reviews.summary: Forchhammer’s copy records dispatch of all fossil pedunculated cirripedes, an enclosed Steenstrup letter about revised distinctions, and a request that Darwin return specimens with names and mark those wanted for his collection.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [15 November 1849], copied from Forchhammer’s book. The date is a note on the copy, and the autograph is not preserved; Camilla dispatch is distinct from later Pomona routing.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Forchhammer’s copied prose is the surviving voice; Steenstrup’s enclosed letter is reported but unavailable.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1273 says Darwin received a letter dated 16 November and was still missing the parcel, so an unlocated next-day clarification may intervene between this 15 November copy and Darwin’s response.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is a strong reverse reply to 1255: “all the fossil peduncalated Cirrhipedes” answers Darwin’s request for fossil/recent material, but receipt of the parcel was not demonstrated.

evidence.quote: I have sent to You all the fossil peduncalated Cirrhipedes

record_reviews.summary: Darwin reports that the cirripede parcel has not arrived, traces the Pomona and London agents, identifies Steenstrup’s Alepas squalicola specimen as especially wanted, and asks Forchhammer to investigate and thank Steenstrup.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 1 December [1849], XML exact day. Body says “I received your letter of Nov. 16th”; the 15 November copy-book date and a missing 16 November clarification must remain distinct.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; the parcel, agents and Steenstrup letter are external/physical inputs.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The body strongly answers an unlocated 16 November Forchhammer letter; it should not be collapsed into a direct 1270 reply without preserving that missing intermediate.

evidence.quote: I received your letter of Nov. 16th a few days ago.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Forchhammer for a 27 April geological letter, says Steenstrup’s specimen was useful, and reports that 33 fossil pedunculated cirripedes are with Sowerby for drawings.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 20 May [1850], XML exact day. The acknowledged 27 April letter is not preserved and its receipt date is not inferred.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Forchhammer’s missing geological letter and Steenstrup’s specimen are acknowledged inputs.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The explicit 27 April letter is a missing antecedent, not 1270 or 1273; no direct packet edge is proposed.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin invites Chambers to call in London on Wednesday between 11 and 12, with a fallback if no answer because of uncertain health and a crowded schedule.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [20 September 1847], XML period date. “Wednesday next” is relative to composition and does not prove a meeting occurred.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; no other voice or enclosure is present.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: This is a social invitation and does not identify the scientific Glen Roy exchange in 1119/1124.

record_reviews.summary: The body begins with the editorial heading “Extract from Letter from C. Darwin to R. Chambers 11 Sept 1847,” then Darwin argues against detritus barriers, distinguishes glacier/iceberg and tidal action, and asks Chambers to level Glen Glastig, Glen Spean and the watershed. P6 asks “Shall you do any levelling?”
record_reviews.date_assessment: Header 11 September 1847; footnote 2 says the handwritten date may read 16 September 1847. Preserve both possibilities. P1 is an editorial copy heading, not Darwin’s body; P2–P7 are the surviving Darwin text.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin is the author of the extracted letter; the heading and editorial notes are not Darwin prose. No MathML survives for the vertical-course/table material.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1124 is Chambers’s 5 October Edinburgh report after finding “two letters” and then a third; Belleville and terrace levels answer the levelling request, but its date and missing two letters prevent same-day assumptions.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The canonical direction 1119→1124 is reversed. 1119 is the outgoing request; any reply edge must be 1124→1119, with the two additional unlocated letters and date ambiguity retained.

record_reviews.summary: Chambers reports that he found two Darwin letters and then received a third, describes Belleville and Kingussie terraces, gives levels near 869/877 and 998 feet, rejects glacier formation of the Glen Roy terraces, and supplies a tabular comparison including 1202, 1203, 1170, 1162, 1090, 1087, 989, 987, 877 and 766.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 5 October 1847 from Edinburgh. “I came home last night” places his return on 4 October, but does not make the letter known to Darwin on the evening of 5 October or establish a response to any unlocated same-day source.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Robert Chambers is the surviving writer. The table is preserved as a body layout/number sequence; CD’s separate annotations are scholarly apparatus and not Chambers’s voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1119 asks about Glen Glastig, Glen Spean, the watershed and levelling; 1124 supplies precisely a field report and measurements, making 1124→1119 the supported direction, subject to the two missing letters.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The distinctive levelling request/report supports 1124 replies_to 1119. The canonical reverse claim must be withdrawn; the response scope is Chambers’s full surviving report, while exact antecedent among Darwin’s two other letters remains unresolved.

evidence.quote: I came home last night and found two letters from you: tonight I receive a third.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Chambers for the hand-level account, says he recommended the instrument in his Instructions, and praises the scale and progress of Chambers’s book and its 30 engravings.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Header [before 17 November 1847], with the body tied to the hand-level account; no exact receipt day is established.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Chambers’s hand-level account and book are acknowledged inputs.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1124 contains terrace measurements but no hand-level wording or instrument reference; the source may be related background, but it does not establish 1160 as a direct reply.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: A specific hand-level input is missing; same Glen Roy subject is insufficient to link 1160 to 1124.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin praises Chambers’s Ancient sea margins, then gives a detailed Glen Roy critique: Milne’s glacier influence, faint Glen Spean terraces, the lines between shelves 2 and 3, buttresses and Darwin’s earlier marine argument.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [June 1848], XML bounded to June 1–30. The date is inferred from receipt of Chambers’s book published between 30 May and 13 June, not an exact day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes; Chambers’s book is the received publication and quoted phrases from it remain external text.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1181, dated 21? June, discusses Chambers’s apology and sea-level theory, but both are Darwin outgoing letters and no direct prompt relation is established.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: The source responds to Chambers’s published book, not a surviving incoming letter; no graph edge is proposed.

proposed_links.reason: Forchhammer’s copy-book says he sent all fossil pedunculated cirripedes and asks Darwin to return and name them; Darwin’s 25 September request specifically asks for fossil/recent specimens to compare with Steenstrup. The copy-book and later routing preserve dispatch versus receipt uncertainty.
proposed_links.response_scope: Whole surviving copy-book paragraph; parcel receipt is not demonstrated.

I have sent to You all the fossil peduncalated Cirrhipedes

proposed_links.reason: Chambers’s 5 October field report answers Darwin’s request for levelling and Glen Glastig/Glen Spean measurements. The date ambiguity on 1119 (11 or possibly 16 September) and Chambers’s statement that two other Darwin letters were also present are retained.
proposed_links.response_scope: Whole surviving Chambers report; exact division among Darwin’s three letters is unresolved.
